thread:
jordan: Heads up — we've got a flood of tenant-level 429 alerts coming from prod-west. Looks like a single customer running a stress test. Should we mute that tenant or tweak the alert? https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/tenant_429_rate
akshay: Which alert exactly? Can you paste the alert rule and a dashboard link?
jordan: Alert is `tenant_429_rate_per_min{job="router"}`. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/router-overview?orgId=1&var-region=prod-west
Logs show repeated `tenant_id=acme-test-42` doing ~10k rps in a short window. Traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/?q=acme-test-42
maria: Yea that's noisy. Two options: 1) short snooze for that tenant (30m) while they finish the test, 2) make the alert resilient to high-cardinality bursts by using a `topk` or using `increase(...)[5m] > X` with `by (tenant)` and a minimum reqs threshold.
leo: +1 for a short snooze first. We should also avoid per-tenant alerts firing on single-tenant storms. Example PromQL to limit cardinality:```
# only alert on top 5 tenants by 429 volume
topk(5, sum by(tenant) (increase(router_response_status{status=429}[5m]))) > 50
```
maria: That looks good. If we bump the >50 threshold to >100 for these regions it will reduce noise but keep signal. If we need to keep per-tenant coverage we can add `unless sum by(tenant) (increase(router_requests_total[5m])) < 100` to ignore tiny tenants.
akshay: I'm fine with a 30m snooze now while we update the rule. @maria can you open a PR for the rule change and include the rationale?
maria: Yep, I'll open the PR and link the runbook. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/alerts/tenant-429
sre-bot: /snooze create --alert tenant_429_rate_per_min --match 'tenant=acme-test-42' --duration 30m
sre-bot: Snooze created: tenant_429_rate_per_min (match: tenant=acme-test-42) until 2111114022. Reason: ongoing customer load test.
leo: Thanks — monitoring the alert noise. If it persists after the PR we'll escalate to change the rule for prod-west permanently. :thumbsup:
